One important area learned in regards to roles is gender identity.� Do we label ourselves as male or female?

Children usually understand their own sex-label by the age of three.� Clothing and hairstyles are the main characteristics a child uses to tell the gender identity of others. This task may seem very simple, but on occasion, unisex clothing and hairstyles, children have to use fine distinctions to complete this.

The development of a stable gender identity usually happens around age five and is the most unchanging of all social identities.�

 Male and  female are based on the biological make-up of the body, however masculine and feminine are determined by our cultural perspective.� Because masculinity and femininity are not determined genetically they can be expressed in a wide variety of ways.
